text:
Recommendation Overview: Adopt a surgical, data-driven approach focused on identifying the top 30-40 flaky tests responsible for the majority of failures, optimizing parallel execution to reduce CI time by at least 25%, and establishing a strict 'Flaky Test Quarantine' rule. The goal is to eliminate trust-breaking flakiness from the main pipeline while reducing CI duration through concurrency improvements, all within a strict two-engineer-week budget.

Week One: Baseline Measurement & Data Collection. Dedicate 0.5 engineer-weeks to instrumenting the test suite. You must capture three data points for every CI run: 1) Test execution time per test (to identify slow tests), 2) Flakiness rate (by forcing re-runs of failed tests locally or via a dedicated 'retry' job that records success/fail on second attempt), and 3) Correlation between failure type and environment instability. The target is to generate a 'Flakiness Heatmap' ranking the top 10% of tests by flakiness score (frequency of pass-on-retry relative to total failures). Do not fix anything yet; the goal is purely diagnostic.

Diagnosis Phase: Uncovering Root Causes. With the heatmap, isolate the specific tests causing the most trust erosion. For each top flaky test, perform a root cause analysis using the '5 Whys' method combined with log review. Common causes in web products include: asynchronous race conditions (missing awaits), shared mutable state between tests, non-deterministic data fixtures, or external service dependencies (e.g., DNS delays, third-party API rate limits). Categorize each failure as either a 'Code Bug', 'Environment Issue', or 'Test Design Flaw'. This step should take 0.5 engineer-weeks. You must document the specific fix required for each top 20 tests.

Prioritized Interventions & Execution Strategy. With limited resources, you cannot fix all 32 flaky tests (8% of 400). Focus on the 'Critical 10': those that fail most frequently and are high-impact. Fix these first. Strategies include: 1) Adding explicit waits/retries for DOM elements, 2) Isolating test data by using unique IDs per run to prevent collisions, 3) Mocking external services deterministically. Each fix should be validated locally before merging. This intensive fixing phase will consume 0.5 engineer-weeks. Concurrently, begin optimizing CI infrastructure by enabling parallel execution across multiple machines or containers for unit and integration tests, which typically offer the largest time savings.

CI Time Optimization & Parallelization. Reduce CI from 45 minutes to <35 minutes. Achieve this by: 1) Running unit tests in parallel (they are fast but numerous), 2) Grouping browser tests by speed and distributing across browsers/devices, 3) Removing redundant tests or merging overlapping assertions. Use caching for dependencies (npm packages, Docker layers). This infrastructure work requires 0.5 engineer-weeks of engineering effort. Ensure that the test runner supports parallel execution out-of-the-box or use tools like GitHub Actions' concurrency features or Jenkins parallel blocks.

Sustainability Rule: Flaky Test Quarantine Policy. Implement a mandatory rule: Any test identified as flaky (passing on retry) is automatically moved to a 'Quarantine' job that does not block the pipeline. Engineers must fix it within 5 days or remove it. This prevents noise from accumulating. Assign ownership: each team member is responsible for fixing their own flaky tests during code reviews. This rule should be enforced via CI gates and developer guidelines, requiring no additional engineering time to maintain once established.

Budget Allocation Summary. Week 1: 0.5 eng-week (measurement). Diagnosis: 0.5 eng-week (analysis). Fixing Critical Flakes: 0.5 eng-week (code changes). CI Optimization: 0.5 eng-week (infrastructure). Total: 2.0 engineer-weeks. This leaves no buffer, so focus must remain tight. Do not attempt to fix low-impact flaky tests; accept them in quarantine until resources allow.

Six-Week Targets. By week six, achieve: 1) Zero flaky tests in the main pipeline (all moved to quarantine or fixed). 2) CI time reduced by at least 20% (to ~36 minutes) through parallelization and caching. 3) 100% of engineers adhere to the Quarantine Policy for new tests. These metrics are measurable via CI logs (flakiness rate = 0%) and pipeline duration reports.

Addressing Constraints & Success Criteria. You measured flakiness before fixing (Week One). Targets are clear: 0% main-pipeline flakiness, <35 min CI time. Interventions were prioritized by impact and cost documented. The sustainability rule is explicit. Deleting tests is only done if behavior is covered elsewhere or gone, ensuring quality isn't compromised.

Final Notes & Caveats. The biggest risk is underestimating the complexity of race conditions in browser tests. If fixes take longer than expected, deprioritize CI optimization and focus solely on fixing the top 5 flaky tests to restore trust. Additionally, ensure that the 'Quarantine' job runs frequently enough to catch regressions without wasting compute. Communication with stakeholders about the 'trust restoration plan' is critical to manage expectations during the transition.
